[42](https://docs.rs#42)
[43](https://docs.rs#43)use proc_macro::TokenStream;
[44](https://docs.rs#44)use proc_macro2::TokenStream as TokenStream2;
[45](https://docs.rs#45)use quote::quote;
[46](https://docs.rs#46)use syn::{parse_macro_input, Attribute, Data, DeriveInput, Fields, Ident, LitStr, Meta, Type};
[47](https://docs.rs#47)
[48](https://docs.rs#48)/// `#[derive(ClosedSet)]` — emit the substrate-wide
[49](https://docs.rs#49)/// [`tatara_lisp::ClosedSet`] impl + the matching [`std::str::FromStr`]
[50](https://docs.rs#50)/// delegation for any enum carrying the closed-set-enum idiom (the
[51](https://docs.rs#51)/// four-piece `ALL` + projection + `Unknown` + `FromStr` shape).
[52](https://docs.rs#52)///
[53](https://docs.rs#53)/// Lifts the 4-line `impl ClosedSet` + 4-line `impl FromStr` boilerplate
[54](https://docs.rs#54)/// that 29+ workspace-wide implementors re-derive byte-for-byte — the
[55](https://docs.rs#55)/// per-implementor content stays at the inherent `ALL` constant and the
[56](https://docs.rs#56)/// inherent projection method (`as_str`, `label`, `prefix`, `marker`,
[57](https://docs.rs#57)/// `keyword`, …), while the trait-impl plumbing collapses onto ONE
[58](https://docs.rs#58)/// derive line.
[59](https://docs.rs#59)///
[60](https://docs.rs#60)/// ## Attributes
[61](https://docs.rs#61)///
[62](https://docs.rs#62)/// - `#[closed_set(via = "as_str")]` — name of the inherent projection
[63](https://docs.rs#63)///   method the trait's [`tatara_lisp::ClosedSet::label`] delegates to.
[64](https://docs.rs#64)///   Defaults to `"label"`. Domain-canonical names
[65](https://docs.rs#65)///   (`tatara_process`'s `as_str`, `tatara_lisp::ast::QuoteForm::prefix`,
[66](https://docs.rs#66)///   `tatara_lisp::error::UnquoteForm::marker`,
[67](https://docs.rs#67)///   `tatara_lisp::error::MacroDefHead::keyword`) stay load-bearing.
[68](https://docs.rs#68)/// - `#[closed_set(unknown = "UnknownX")]` — name of the
[69](https://docs.rs#69)///   per-implementor `Unknown` carrier struct
[70](https://docs.rs#70)///   [`tatara_lisp::ClosedSet::make_unknown`] constructs. Defaults to
[71](https://docs.rs#71)///   `"Unknown{EnumName}"` — matches the substrate-wide naming
[72](https://docs.rs#72)///   convention (`UnknownChannelKind` for `ChannelKind`).
[73](https://docs.rs#73)/// - `#[closed_set(no_from_str)]` — suppress the generated
[74](https://docs.rs#74)///   `impl FromStr`. Use for enums that already carry a bespoke
[75](https://docs.rs#75)///   `FromStr` shape (e.g. [`tatara_lisp::error::CompilerSpecIoStage`]'s
[76](https://docs.rs#76)///   compound `"{operation}: {label}"` key, which keys on a projection
[77](https://docs.rs#77)///   PAIR rather than a single label).
[78](https://docs.rs#78)/// - `#[closed_set(generate_unknown)]` /
[79](https://docs.rs#79)///   `#[closed_set(generate_unknown = "<label>")]` — emit the
[80](https://docs.rs#80)///   `pub struct Unknown{EnumName}(pub String)` parse-rejection
[81](https://docs.rs#81)///   carrier alongside the trait impl. The carrier derives
[82](https://docs.rs#82)///   `Debug + Clone + PartialEq + Eq + thiserror::Error` and renders
[83](https://docs.rs#83)///   `#[error("unknown <label>: {0}")]`. The bare form derives
[84](https://docs.rs#84)///   `<label>` by spacing the PascalCase enum name into lowercase
[85](https://docs.rs#85)///   words (`ChannelKind` → "channel kind", `ReplacementPolicy` →
[86](https://docs.rs#86)///   "replacement policy"); the `= "..."` form pins an explicit label
[87](https://docs.rs#87)///   for irregular cases (`MacroDefHead` wants "macro definition
[88](https://docs.rs#88)///   head" rather than the auto-derived "macro def head";
[89](https://docs.rs#89)///   `MustReachPhase` wants "must-reach phase"). The 3-line
[90](https://docs.rs#90)///   `pub struct Unknown{EnumName}(pub String)` declaration (plus its
[91](https://docs.rs#91)///   thiserror derives + `#[error(...)]` annotation) is the
[92](https://docs.rs#92)///   substrate-wide closed-set-enum idiom's last hand-rolled piece;
[93](https://docs.rs#93)///   this attribute collapses it onto the derive so a 40+ enum
[94](https://docs.rs#94)///   cohort emits the carrier through ONE generative shape rather
[95](https://docs.rs#95)///   than re-deriving the boilerplate at each declaration site.
[96](https://docs.rs#96)/// - `#[closed_set(display)]` — emit the substrate-wide
[97](https://docs.rs#97)///   `impl ::core::fmt::Display for $name { f.write_str(Self::$via(*self)) }`
[98](https://docs.rs#98)///   block alongside the trait impl. The 5-line Display block (the
[99](https://docs.rs#99)///   `impl fmt::Display`, the `fn fmt`, the `f.write_str(self.$via())`
[100](https://docs.rs#100)///   body) appears 28+ times across `tatara-process` /
[101](https://docs.rs#101)///   `tatara-lisp` byte-for-byte — every closed-set carrier on a
[102](https://docs.rs#102)///   PascalCase wire-format axis composes its operator-facing
[103](https://docs.rs#103)///   diagnostic through Display rather than through a hard-coded
[104](https://docs.rs#104)///   literal that would silently rot when a variant gets renamed.
[105](https://docs.rs#105)///   The attribute collapses the 5-line block onto ONE flag so the
[106](https://docs.rs#106)///   `as_str` ⇄ Display ⇄ `FromStr` triad emits through ONE
[107](https://docs.rs#107)///   generative shape per closed-set enum.
[108](https://docs.rs#108)///   The emission requires `Self: ::core::marker::Copy` (the
[109](https://docs.rs#109)///   `ClosedSet` trait already requires it). Set the flag in
[110](https://docs.rs#110)///   combination with `via` to pin Display onto the inherent
[111](https://docs.rs#111)///   projection rather than the trait method; without the flag the
[112](https://docs.rs#112)///   implementor keeps its hand-rolled Display block (e.g. for a
[113](https://docs.rs#113)///   bespoke Display shape like
[114](https://docs.rs#114)///   [`tatara_process::lifetime_clock::TerminateReason`]'s
[115](https://docs.rs#115)///   structured-reason formatter).
[116](https://docs.rs#116)///
[117](https://docs.rs#117)/// ## Implementor requirements
[118](https://docs.rs#118)///
[119](https://docs.rs#119)/// The derive expects the enum to expose at the inherent surface:
[120](https://docs.rs#120)///
[121](https://docs.rs#121)/// 1. `pub const ALL: [Self; N] = [...]` — forced-arity array literal.
[122](https://docs.rs#122)/// 2. A `fn projection(self) -> &'static str` method whose name matches
[123](https://docs.rs#123)///    `via` (defaults to `label`).
[124](https://docs.rs#124)/// 3. A `pub struct UnknownX(pub String)` in the same module whose name
[125](https://docs.rs#125)///    matches `unknown` (defaults to `Unknown{EnumName}`) — UNLESS
[126](https://docs.rs#126)///    `#[closed_set(generate_unknown)]` is set, in which case the
[127](https://docs.rs#127)///    derive emits the struct itself.
[128](https://docs.rs#128)///
[129](https://docs.rs#129)/// The derive emits:
[130](https://docs.rs#130)///
[131](https://docs.rs#131)/// ```ignore
[132](https://docs.rs#132)/// impl ::tatara_lisp::ClosedSet for $name {
[133](https://docs.rs#133)///     const ALL: &'static [Self] = &Self::ALL;
[134](https://docs.rs#134)///     type Unknown = $unknown;
[135](https://docs.rs#135)///     fn label(self) -> &'static str { Self::$via(self) }
[136](https://docs.rs#136)///     fn make_unknown(s: &str) -> Self::Unknown {
[137](https://docs.rs#137)///         $unknown(::std::string::String::from(s))
[138](https://docs.rs#138)///     }
[139](https://docs.rs#139)/// }
[140](https://docs.rs#140)///
[141](https://docs.rs#141)/// impl ::core::str::FromStr for $name {
[142](https://docs.rs#142)///     type Err = $unknown;
[143](https://docs.rs#143)///     fn from_str(s: &str) -> ::core::result::Result<Self, Self::Err> {
[144](https://docs.rs#144)///         <Self as ::tatara_lisp::ClosedSet>::parse_label(s)
[145](https://docs.rs#145)///     }
[146](https://docs.rs#146)/// }
[147](https://docs.rs#147)/// ```
[148](https://docs.rs#148)///
[149](https://docs.rs#149)/// ## Theory grounding
[150](https://docs.rs#150)///
[151](https://docs.rs#151)/// THEORY.md §VI.1 — generation over composition; the derive IS the
[152](https://docs.rs#152)/// generative shape — new closed-set enums add ONE `#[derive(ClosedSet)]`
[153](https://docs.rs#153)/// line + the attribute that names their inherent projection method
[154](https://docs.rs#154)/// instead of re-deriving the eight-line `impl ClosedSet` + `impl FromStr`
[155](https://docs.rs#155)/// pair byte-for-byte. The per-implementor `Unknown` carrier stays
[156](https://docs.rs#156)/// hand-rolled (its `#[error("unknown <thing>: {0}")]` annotation IS
[157](https://docs.rs#157)/// per-implementor content), but the trait-impl plumbing it threads
[158](https://docs.rs#158)/// through collapses onto the derive.
[159](https://docs.rs#159)#[proc_macro_derive(ClosedSet, attributes(closed_set))]
[160](https://docs.rs#160)pub fn derive_closed_set(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
[161](https://docs.rs#161)    let input = parse_macro_input!(input as DeriveInput);
[162](https://docs.rs#162)    let name = input.ident.clone();
[163](https://docs.rs#163)
[164](https://docs.rs#164)    if !matches!(input.data, Data::Enum(_)) {
[165](https://docs.rs#165)        return syn::Error::new_spanned(
[166](https://docs.rs#166)            &name,
[167](https://docs.rs#167)            "ClosedSet may only be derived on enums (the closed-set-enum idiom)",
[168](https://docs.rs#168)        )
[169](https://docs.rs#169)        .to_compile_error()
[170](https://docs.rs#170)        .into();
[171](https://docs.rs#171)    }
[172](https://docs.rs#172)
[173](https://docs.rs#173)    let cfg = match parse_closed_set_attrs(&input.attrs, &name) {
[174](https://docs.rs#174)        Ok(c) => c,
[175](https://docs.rs#175)        Err(err) => return err.to_compile_error().into(),
[176](https://docs.rs#176)    };
[177](https://docs.rs#177)
[178](https://docs.rs#178)    let via_ident = Ident::new(&cfg.via, name.span());
[179](https://docs.rs#179)    let unknown_ident = Ident::new(&cfg.unknown, name.span());
[180](https://docs.rs#180)
[181](https://docs.rs#181)    // Resolve the SET_LABEL the derive threads into BOTH the trait's
[182](https://docs.rs#182)    // `const SET_LABEL` AND the carrier's `#[error("unknown <label>:
[183](https://docs.rs#183)    // {0}")]` annotation. The priority chain is the typed-escape-hatch
[184](https://docs.rs#184)    // shape every other axis on this derive carries:
[185](https://docs.rs#185)    //   1. `#[closed_set(set_label = "...")]` — explicit override at
[186](https://docs.rs#186)    //      the trait surface, independent of the carrier's annotation.
[187](https://docs.rs#187)    //      No production implementor reaches for this today; the axis
[188](https://docs.rs#188)    //      exists for the degenerate case where an implementor wants
[189](https://docs.rs#189)    //      to bind the trait's set name independently of the carrier's
[190](https://docs.rs#190)    //      diagnostic label (a future structured-diagnostic carrier
[191](https://docs.rs#191)    //      that wraps a richer payload than `pub String`).
[192](https://docs.rs#192)    //   2. `#[closed_set(generate_unknown = "<label>")]` — the same
[193](https://docs.rs#193)    //      label the carrier's `#[error(...)]` annotation already
[194](https://docs.rs#194)    //      pins, threaded through to the trait surface so the two
[195](https://docs.rs#195)    //      surfaces emit from ONE generative origin. Covers irregular
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    //      labels (`MacroDefHead` → "macro definition head",
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    //      `MustReachPhase` → "must-reach phase") whose operator-
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    //      pinned wording diverges from the auto-derived projection.
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    //   3. `#[closed_set(generate_unknown)]` / `Skip` — auto-derive
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    //      via `pascal_to_spaced_lowercase` on the enum name. Covers
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    //      the regular case (`ChannelKind` → "channel kind",
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    //      `ReplacementPolicy` → "replacement policy"); also the
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    //      fallback for `Skip` so an implementor that hand-rolls the
[204](https://docs.rs#204)    //      carrier still gets a typed SET_LABEL without touching the
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    //      derive attribute surface.
[206](https://docs.rs#206)    let set_label = match (&cfg.set_label, &cfg.generate_unknown) {
[207](https://docs.rs#207)        (Some(explicit), _) => explicit.clone(),
[208](https://docs.rs#208)        (None, GenerateUnknown::Explicit(label)) => label.clone(),
[209](https://docs.rs#209)        (None, GenerateUnknown::Auto | GenerateUnknown::Skip) => {
[210](https://docs.rs#210)            pascal_to_spaced_lowercase(&name.to_string())
[211](https://docs.rs#211)        }
[212](https://docs.rs#212)    };
[213](https://docs.rs#213)
[214](https://docs.rs#214)    let from_str_impl = if cfg.no_from_str {
[215](https://docs.rs#215)        TokenStream2::new()
[216](https://docs.rs#216)    } else {
[217](https://docs.rs#217)        quote! {
[218](https://docs.rs#218)            impl ::core::str::FromStr for #name {
[219](https://docs.rs#219)                type Err = #unknown_ident;
[220](https://docs.rs#220)                fn from_str(
[221](https://docs.rs#221)                    s: &::core::primitive::str,
[222](https://docs.rs#222)                ) -> ::core::result::Result<Self, Self::Err> {
[223](https://docs.rs#223)                    <Self as ::tatara_lisp::ClosedSet>::parse_label(s)
[224](https://docs.rs#224)                }
[225](https://docs.rs#225)            }
[226](https://docs.rs#226)        }
[227](https://docs.rs#227)    };
[228](https://docs.rs#228)
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    let unknown_struct_decl = match &cfg.generate_unknown {
[230](https://docs.rs#230)        GenerateUnknown::Skip => TokenStream2::new(),
[231](https://docs.rs#231)        GenerateUnknown::Auto | GenerateUnknown::Explicit(_) => {
[232](https://docs.rs#232)            // The carrier's `#[error(...)]` annotation reads from the
[233](https://docs.rs#233)            // SAME resolved `set_label` the trait const reads from —
[234](https://docs.rs#234)            // a regression at one site cannot drift from the other,
[235](https://docs.rs#235)            // because both flow from the SAME local binding.
[236](https://docs.rs#236)            emit_unknown_struct(&unknown_ident, &set_label)
[237](https://docs.rs#237)        }
[238](https://docs.rs#238)    };
[239](https://docs.rs#239)
[240](https://docs.rs#240)    let display_impl = if cfg.display {
[241](https://docs.rs#241)        quote! {
[242](https://docs.rs#242)            impl ::core::fmt::Display for #name {
[243](https://docs.rs#243)                fn fmt(
[244](https://docs.rs#244)                    &self,
[245](https://docs.rs#245)                    f: &mut ::core::fmt::Formatter<'_>,
[246](https://docs.rs#246)                ) -> ::core::fmt::Result {
[247](https://docs.rs#247)                    f.write_str(Self::#via_ident(*self))
[248](https://docs.rs#248)                }
[249](https://docs.rs#249)            }
[250](https://docs.rs#250)        }
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    } else {
[252](https://docs.rs#252)        TokenStream2::new()
[253](https://docs.rs#253)    };
[254](https://docs.rs#254)
[255](https://docs.rs#255)    let expanded = quote! {
[256](https://docs.rs#256)        impl ::tatara_lisp::ClosedSet for #name {
[257](https://docs.rs#257)            const ALL: &'static [Self] = &Self::ALL;
[258](https://docs.rs#258)            const SET_LABEL: &'static ::core::primitive::str = #set_label;
[259](https://docs.rs#259)            type Unknown = #unknown_ident;
[260](https://docs.rs#260)            fn label(self) -> &'static ::core::primitive::str {
[261](https://docs.rs#261)                Self::#via_ident(self)
[262](https://docs.rs#262)            }
[263](https://docs.rs#263)            fn make_unknown(
[264](https://docs.rs#264)                s: &::core::primitive::str,
[265](https://docs.rs#265)            ) -> Self::Unknown {
[266](https://docs.rs#266)                #unknown_ident(::std::string::String::from(s))
[267](https://docs.rs#267)            }
[268](https://docs.rs#268)        }
[269](https://docs.rs#269)
[270](https://docs.rs#270)        #from_str_impl
[271](https://docs.rs#271)
[272](https://docs.rs#272)        #unknown_struct_decl
[273](https://docs.rs#273)
[274](https://docs.rs#274)        #display_impl
[275](https://docs.rs#275)    };
[276](https://docs.rs#276)
[277](https://docs.rs#277)    expanded.into()
[278](https://docs.rs#278)}
[279](https://docs.rs#279)
[280](https://docs.rs#280)/// Emit the `pub struct UnknownX(pub String)` parse-rejection carrier
[281](https://docs.rs#281)/// for `#[closed_set(generate_unknown[ = "label"])]`. The shape is the
[282](https://docs.rs#282)/// substrate-wide closed-set-enum carrier idiom: `Debug + Clone +
[283](https://docs.rs#283)/// PartialEq + Eq + thiserror::Error` derives with an
[284](https://docs.rs#284)/// `#[error("unknown <label>: {0}")]` annotation that surfaces the
[285](https://docs.rs#285)/// offending input verbatim. Lifted into ONE helper so every
[286](https://docs.rs#286)/// generated carrier flows through ONE composition site — a
[287](https://docs.rs#287)/// regression that drifts the derive set or the message shape
[288](https://docs.rs#288)/// between two generated carriers is structurally impossible.
[289](https://docs.rs#289)fn emit_unknown_struct(unknown_ident: &Ident, label: &str) -> TokenStream2 {
[290](https://docs.rs#290)    let msg = format!("unknown {label}: {{0}}");
[291](https://docs.rs#291)    quote! {
[292](https://docs.rs#292)        #[derive(
[293](https://docs.rs#293)            ::core::fmt::Debug,
[294](https://docs.rs#294)            ::core::clone::Clone,
[295](https://docs.rs#295)            ::core::cmp::PartialEq,
[296](https://docs.rs#296)            ::core::cmp::Eq,
[297](https://docs.rs#297)            ::thiserror::Error,
[298](https://docs.rs#298)        )]
[299](https://docs.rs#299)        #[error(#msg)]
[300](https://docs.rs#300)        pub struct #unknown_ident(pub ::std::string::String);
[301](https://docs.rs#301)    }
[302](https://docs.rs#302)}
[303](https://docs.rs#303)
[304](https://docs.rs#304)/// Project a PascalCase identifier into the substrate-wide
[305](https://docs.rs#305)/// spaced-lowercase label `#[closed_set(generate_unknown)]` threads
[306](https://docs.rs#306)/// into the auto-derived `#[error("unknown <label>: {0}")]`
[307](https://docs.rs#307)/// annotation. Mirrors the workspace-wide hand-rolled convention
[308](https://docs.rs#308)/// across 40+ closed-set carriers (`ChannelKind` →
[309](https://docs.rs#309)/// "channel kind", `ReplacementPolicy` → "replacement policy",
[310](https://docs.rs#310)/// `CompilerSpecIoStage` → "compiler spec io stage").
[311](https://docs.rs#311)///
[312](https://docs.rs#312)/// A run of contiguous uppercase characters projects byte-for-byte to
[313](https://docs.rs#313)/// lowercase without inserting interior spaces; a space is emitted
[314](https://docs.rs#314)/// only at the lowercase→uppercase boundary. Irregular labels
[315](https://docs.rs#315)/// (`MacroDefHead` → "macro definition head" with "Def" expanded;
[316](https://docs.rs#316)/// `MustReachPhase` → "must-reach phase" with a hyphen) fall outside
[317](https://docs.rs#317)/// the projection's codomain and require the explicit
[318](https://docs.rs#318)/// `#[closed_set(generate_unknown = "...")]` override.
[319](https://docs.rs#319)fn pascal_to_spaced_lowercase(name: &str) -> String {
[320](https://docs.rs#320)    let mut out = String::with_capacity(name.len() + 2);
[321](https://docs.rs#321)    let mut prev_was_lower = false;
[322](https://docs.rs#322)    for c in name.chars() {
[323](https://docs.rs#323)        if c.is_ascii_uppercase() {
[324](https://docs.rs#324)            if prev_was_lower {
[325](https://docs.rs#325)                out.push(' ');
[326](https://docs.rs#326)            }
[327](https://docs.rs#327)            out.push(c.to_ascii_lowercase());
[328](https://docs.rs#328)            prev_was_lower = false;
[329](https://docs.rs#329)        } else {
[330](https://docs.rs#330)            out.push(c);
[331](https://docs.rs#331)            prev_was_lower = c.is_ascii_lowercase();
[332](https://docs.rs#332)        }
[333](https://docs.rs#333)    }
[334](https://docs.rs#334)    out
[335](https://docs.rs#335)}
[336](https://docs.rs#336)
[337](https://docs.rs#337)#[cfg(test)]
[338](https://docs.rs#338)mod pascal_to_spaced_lowercase_tests {
[339](https://docs.rs#339)    use super::pascal_to_spaced_lowercase;
[340](https://docs.rs#340)
[341](https://docs.rs#341)    #[test]
[342](https://docs.rs#342)    fn regular_two_word_names_split_at_the_word_boundary() {
[343](https://docs.rs#343)        // The bread-and-butter case across 30+ closed-set carriers —
[344](https://docs.rs#344)        // PascalCase with a single internal capital splits at the
[345](https://docs.rs#345)        // capital. The retrofit cohort
[346](https://docs.rs#346)        // (`ChannelKind`/`ArtifactKind`/`ReportFormat`/`ExportTrigger`)
[347](https://docs.rs#347)        // all live in this case so the auto-derived label matches
[348](https://docs.rs#348)        // the workspace-wide convention without an explicit override.
[349](https://docs.rs#349)        assert_eq!(pascal_to_spaced_lowercase("ChannelKind"), "channel kind");
[350](https://docs.rs#350)        assert_eq!(pascal_to_spaced_lowercase("ArtifactKind"), "artifact kind");
[351](https://docs.rs#351)        assert_eq!(pascal_to_spaced_lowercase("ReportFormat"), "report format");
[352](https://docs.rs#352)        assert_eq!(
[353](https://docs.rs#353)            pascal_to_spaced_lowercase("ExportTrigger"),
[354](https://docs.rs#354)            "export trigger",
[355](https://docs.rs#355)        );
[356](https://docs.rs#356)        assert_eq!(
[357](https://docs.rs#357)            pascal_to_spaced_lowercase("ReplacementPolicy"),
[358](https://docs.rs#358)            "replacement policy",
[359](https://docs.rs#359)        );
[360](https://docs.rs#360)    }
[361](https://docs.rs#361)
[362](https://docs.rs#362)    #[test]
[363](https://docs.rs#363)    fn three_word_names_split_at_every_word_boundary() {
[364](https://docs.rs#364)        // Closed-set names with three PascalCase tokens
[365](https://docs.rs#365)        // (`CompilerSpecIoStage`, `OptimizationDirection`,
[366](https://docs.rs#366)        // `ConvergencePointType`) split at every lowercase→uppercase
[367](https://docs.rs#367)        // boundary. The split is internal — the trailing PascalCase
[368](https://docs.rs#368)        // tokens stay as separate words rather than collapsing into
[369](https://docs.rs#369)        // the previous one.
[370](https://docs.rs#370)        assert_eq!(
[371](https://docs.rs#371)            pascal_to_spaced_lowercase("OptimizationDirection"),
[372](https://docs.rs#372)            "optimization direction",
[373](https://docs.rs#373)        );
[374](https://docs.rs#374)        assert_eq!(
[375](https://docs.rs#375)            pascal_to_spaced_lowercase("ConvergencePointType"),
[376](https://docs.rs#376)            "convergence point type",

[378](https://docs.rs#378)    }
[379](https://docs.rs#379)
[380](https://docs.rs#380)    #[test]
[381](https://docs.rs#381)    fn contiguous_uppercase_runs_collapse_to_lowercase_without_inner_spaces() {
[382](https://docs.rs#382)        // Acronyms run together rather than fan out per letter —
[383](https://docs.rs#383)        // `CompilerSpecIoStage` projects "compiler spec io stage"
[384](https://docs.rs#384)        // (the "Io" run stays as "io" rather than "i o"). Pinned by
[385](https://docs.rs#385)        // the substrate-wide hand-rolled labels:
[386](https://docs.rs#386)        // `error.rs`'s `UnknownCompilerSpecIoStage` carries the
[387](https://docs.rs#387)        // message "unknown compiler spec io stage: {0}" verbatim, and
[388](https://docs.rs#388)        // the auto-derive must match it bit-for-bit so a retrofit
[389](https://docs.rs#389)        // doesn't drift the operator-facing wording.
[390](https://docs.rs#390)        assert_eq!(
[391](https://docs.rs#391)            pascal_to_spaced_lowercase("CompilerSpecIoStage"),
[392](https://docs.rs#392)            "compiler spec io stage",

[394](https://docs.rs#394)    }
[395](https://docs.rs#395)
[396](https://docs.rs#396)    #[test]
[397](https://docs.rs#397)    fn single_word_names_stay_lowercase_with_no_spaces() {
[398](https://docs.rs#398)        // A single PascalCase token (no internal capital) projects
[399](https://docs.rs#399)        // to a single lowercase word — no leading space, no
[400](https://docs.rs#400)        // mid-word split. Covers degenerate-but-valid cases like a
[401](https://docs.rs#401)        // future `Signal` or `Kind` enum name.
[402](https://docs.rs#402)        assert_eq!(pascal_to_spaced_lowercase("Signal"), "signal");
[403](https://docs.rs#403)        assert_eq!(pascal_to_spaced_lowercase("Kind"), "kind");
[404](https://docs.rs#404)    }
[405](https://docs.rs#405)
[406](https://docs.rs#406)    #[test]
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    fn empty_input_projects_to_empty_string() {
[408](https://docs.rs#408)        // Empty-input contract — projecting `""` yields `""` rather
[409](https://docs.rs#409)        // than a leading space or a panic. Defensive case the
[410](https://docs.rs#410)        // attribute parser shouldn't reach (the derive runs on a
[411](https://docs.rs#411)        // named enum), but pinning it here keeps the helper's
[412](https://docs.rs#412)        // contract independent of the caller's discipline.
[413](https://docs.rs#413)        assert_eq!(pascal_to_spaced_lowercase(""), "");
[414](https://docs.rs#414)    }
[415](https://docs.rs#415)}
[416](https://docs.rs#416)
[417](https://docs.rs#417)struct ClosedSetCfg {
[418](https://docs.rs#418)    via: String,
[419](https://docs.rs#419)    unknown: String,
[420](https://docs.rs#420)    no_from_str: bool,
[421](https://docs.rs#421)    generate_unknown: GenerateUnknown,
[422](https://docs.rs#422)    /// `#[closed_set(display)]` — emit the substrate-wide
[423](https://docs.rs#423)    /// `impl fmt::Display { f.write_str(Self::$via(*self)) }` block.
[424](https://docs.rs#424)    /// 28+ workspace-wide closed-set enums on PascalCase wire-format
[425](https://docs.rs#425)    /// axes (the `as_str ⇄ Display ⇄ FromStr` triad) re-derive this
[426](https://docs.rs#426)    /// 5-line block byte-for-byte; flipping the flag at the derive
[427](https://docs.rs#427)    /// site collapses the block onto ONE generative shape.
[428](https://docs.rs#428)    display: bool,
[429](https://docs.rs#429)    /// `#[closed_set(set_label = "...")]` — explicit override for the
[430](https://docs.rs#430)    /// trait's [`tatara_lisp::ClosedSet::SET_LABEL`] const. Defaults
[431](https://docs.rs#431)    /// to the label `#[closed_set(generate_unknown[ = "..."])]`
[432](https://docs.rs#432)    /// already pinned (or the auto-derived
[433](https://docs.rs#433)    /// `pascal_to_spaced_lowercase(name)` for the bare / `Skip`
[434](https://docs.rs#434)    /// cases) so the trait surface and the carrier's `#[error(...)]`
[435](https://docs.rs#435)    /// annotation emit from ONE generative origin. The override
[436](https://docs.rs#436)    /// exists for the degenerate case where an implementor wants to
[437](https://docs.rs#437)    /// bind the trait's set name independently of the carrier's
[438](https://docs.rs#438)    /// diagnostic label (a future structured-diagnostic carrier that
[439](https://docs.rs#439)    /// wraps a richer payload than `pub String`) — no production
[440](https://docs.rs#440)    /// implementor reaches for it today.
[441](https://docs.rs#441)    set_label: Option<String>,
[442](https://docs.rs#442)}
[443](https://docs.rs#443)
[444](https://docs.rs#444)/// `#[closed_set(generate_unknown[ = "label"])]` parse outcome.
[445](https://docs.rs#445)///
[446](https://docs.rs#446)/// `Skip` keeps the existing convention (implementor hand-rolls the
[447](https://docs.rs#447)/// `pub struct UnknownX(pub String)` carrier alongside the enum).
[448](https://docs.rs#448)/// `Auto` emits the carrier with the spaced-lowercase projection of
[449](https://docs.rs#449)/// the enum name as the `#[error(...)]` label. `Explicit(label)` emits
[450](https://docs.rs#450)/// the carrier with an operator-pinned label that overrides the
[451](https://docs.rs#451)/// PascalCase split (for irregular cases like `MacroDefHead` →
[452](https://docs.rs#452)/// "macro definition head").
[453](https://docs.rs#453)enum GenerateUnknown {
[454](https://docs.rs#454)    Skip,
[455](https://docs.rs#455)    Auto,
[456](https://docs.rs#456)    Explicit(String),
[457](https://docs.rs#457)}
[458](https://docs.rs#458)
[459](https://docs.rs#459)fn parse_closed_set_attrs(attrs: &[Attribute], name: &Ident) -> syn::Result<ClosedSetCfg> {
[460](https://docs.rs#460)    let mut via: Option<String> = None;
[461](https://docs.rs#461)    let mut unknown: Option<String> = None;
[462](https://docs.rs#462)    let mut no_from_str = false;
[463](https://docs.rs#463)    let mut generate_unknown = GenerateUnknown::Skip;
[464](https://docs.rs#464)    let mut display = false;
[465](https://docs.rs#465)    let mut set_label: Option<String> = None;
[466](https://docs.rs#466)    for attr in attrs {
[467](https://docs.rs#467)        if !attr.path().is_ident("closed_set") {
[468](https://docs.rs#468)            continue;
[469](https://docs.rs#469)        }
[470](https://docs.rs#470)        let Meta::List(list) = &attr.meta else {
[471](https://docs.rs#471)            continue;
[472](https://docs.rs#472)        };
[473](https://docs.rs#473)        list.parse_nested_meta(|meta| {
[474](https://docs.rs#474)            if meta.path.is_ident("via") {
[475](https://docs.rs#475)                let value = meta.value()?;
[476](https://docs.rs#476)                let s: LitStr = value.parse()?;
[477](https://docs.rs#477)                via = Some(s.value());
[478](https://docs.rs#478)                Ok(())
[479](https://docs.rs#479)            } else if meta.path.is_ident("unknown") {
[480](https://docs.rs#480)                let value = meta.value()?;
[481](https://docs.rs#481)                let s: LitStr = value.parse()?;
[482](https://docs.rs#482)                unknown = Some(s.value());
[483](https://docs.rs#483)                Ok(())
[484](https://docs.rs#484)            } else if meta.path.is_ident("no_from_str") {
[485](https://docs.rs#485)                no_from_str = true;
[486](https://docs.rs#486)                Ok(())
[487](https://docs.rs#487)            } else if meta.path.is_ident("generate_unknown") {
[488](https://docs.rs#488)                // Both bare `generate_unknown` (auto-derived label)
[489](https://docs.rs#489)                // and `generate_unknown = "explicit label"` (pinned
[490](https://docs.rs#490)                // label) sit on ONE attribute key — the parser
[491](https://docs.rs#491)                // dispatches on whether `meta.value()` succeeds so the
[492](https://docs.rs#492)                // attribute surface stays single-keyed (no
[493](https://docs.rs#493)                // `auto_label`/`label` bifurcation that would force
[494](https://docs.rs#494)                // the operator to think about which of two
[495](https://docs.rs#495)                // attributes is canonical).
[496](https://docs.rs#496)                generate_unknown = match meta.value() {
[497](https://docs.rs#497)                    Ok(value) => {
[498](https://docs.rs#498)                        let s: LitStr = value.parse()?;
[499](https://docs.rs#499)                        GenerateUnknown::Explicit(s.value())
[500](https://docs.rs#500)                    }
[501](https://docs.rs#501)                    Err(_) => GenerateUnknown::Auto,
[502](https://docs.rs#502)                };
[503](https://docs.rs#503)                Ok(())
[504](https://docs.rs#504)            } else if meta.path.is_ident("display") {
[505](https://docs.rs#505)                display = true;
[506](https://docs.rs#506)                Ok(())
[507](https://docs.rs#507)            } else if meta.path.is_ident("set_label") {
[508](https://docs.rs#508)                let value = meta.value()?;
[509](https://docs.rs#509)                let s: LitStr = value.parse()?;
[510](https://docs.rs#510)                set_label = Some(s.value());
[511](https://docs.rs#511)                Ok(())
[512](https://docs.rs#512)            } else {
[513](https://docs.rs#513)                Err(meta.error(
[514](https://docs.rs#514)                    "unknown #[closed_set(...)] key — expected `via`, `unknown`, `no_from_str`, `generate_unknown`, `display`, or `set_label`",
[515](https://docs.rs#515)                ))
[516](https://docs.rs#516)            }
[517](https://docs.rs#517)        })?;
[518](https://docs.rs#518)    }
[519](https://docs.rs#519)    Ok(ClosedSetCfg {
[520](https://docs.rs#520)        via: via.unwrap_or_else(|| "label".to_string()),
[521](https://docs.rs#521)        unknown: unknown.unwrap_or_else(|| format!("Unknown{name}")),
[522](https://docs.rs#522)        no_from_str,
[523](https://docs.rs#523)        generate_unknown,
[524](https://docs.rs#524)        display,
[525](https://docs.rs#525)        set_label,
[526](https://docs.rs#526)    })
[527](https://docs.rs#527)}
[528](https://docs.rs#528)
[529](https://docs.rs#529)#[proc_macro_derive(TataraDomain, attributes(tatara))]
[530](https://docs.rs#530)pub fn derive_tatara_domain(input: TokenStream) -> TokenStream {
[531](https://docs.rs#531)    let input = parse_macro_input!(input as DeriveInput);
[532](https://docs.rs#532)    let name = input.ident.clone();
[533](https://docs.rs#533)    let keyword =
[534](https://docs.rs#534)        extract_keyword(&input.attrs).unwrap_or_else(|| default_keyword(&name.to_string()));
[535](https://docs.rs#535)
[536](https://docs.rs#536)    let fields = match &input.data {
[537](https://docs.rs#537)        Data::Struct(s) => match &s.fields {
[538](https://docs.rs#538)            Fields::Named(n) => &n.named,
[539](https://docs.rs#539)            _ => {
[540](https://docs.rs#540)                return syn::Error::new_spanned(
[541](https://docs.rs#541)                    &name,
[542](https://docs.rs#542)                    "TataraDomain requires a struct with named fields",
[543](https://docs.rs#543)                )
[544](https://docs.rs#544)                .to_compile_error()
[545](https://docs.rs#545)                .into();
[546](https://docs.rs#546)            }
[547](https://docs.rs#547)        },
[548](https://docs.rs#548)        _ => {
[549](https://docs.rs#549)            return syn::Error::new_spanned(&name, "TataraDomain may only be derived on structs")
[550](https://docs.rs#550)                .to_compile_error()
[551](https://docs.rs#551)                .into();
[552](https://docs.rs#552)        }
[553](https://docs.rs#553)    };
[554](https://docs.rs#554)
[555](https://docs.rs#555)    let mut field_inits: Vec<TokenStream2> = Vec::with_capacity(fields.len());
[556](https://docs.rs#556)    let mut allowed_keys: Vec<String> = Vec::with_capacity(fields.len());
[557](https://docs.rs#557)    for field in fields {
[558](https://docs.rs#558)        let ident = field.ident.as_ref().expect("named field");
[559](https://docs.rs#559)        let kebab = snake_to_kebab(&ident.to_string());
[560](https://docs.rs#560)        let has_default = has_serde_default(field);
[561](https://docs.rs#561)        match extractor_for(&field.ty, &kebab, has_default) {
[562](https://docs.rs#562)            Ok(extract) => field_inits.push(quote! { #ident: #extract }),
[563](https://docs.rs#563)            Err(err) => {
[564](https://docs.rs#564)                return syn::Error::new_spanned(&field.ty, err)
[565](https://docs.rs#565)                    .to_compile_error()
[566](https://docs.rs#566)                    .into();
[567](https://docs.rs#567)            }
[568](https://docs.rs#568)        }
[569](https://docs.rs#569)        allowed_keys.push(kebab);
[570](https://docs.rs#570)    }
[571](https://docs.rs#571)
[572](https://docs.rs#572)    let allowed_lits = allowed_keys.iter().map(|k| quote! { #k });
[573](https://docs.rs#573)
[574](https://docs.rs#574)    let expanded = quote! {
[575](https://docs.rs#575)        impl ::tatara_lisp::domain::TataraDomain for #name {
[576](https://docs.rs#576)            const KEYWORD: &'static str = #keyword;
[577](https://docs.rs#577)
[578](https://docs.rs#578)            fn compile_from_args(
[579](https://docs.rs#579)                args: &[::tatara_lisp::Sexp],
[580](https://docs.rs#580)            ) -> ::tatara_lisp::Result<Self> {
[581](https://docs.rs#581)                const __TATARA_ALLOWED_KEYWORDS: &[&::core::primitive::str] = &[
[582](https://docs.rs#582)                    #(#allowed_lits),*
[583](https://docs.rs#583)                ];
[584](https://docs.rs#584)                // The fused typed-entry kwargs gate: parse `:k v :k v …` AND
[585](https://docs.rs#585)                // assert every key sits in the static allowed-set, in ONE
[586](https://docs.rs#586)                // call. Before this lift the derive emitted the two-call
[587](https://docs.rs#587)                // sequence (`parse_kwargs` + `reject_unknown_kwargs`)
[588](https://docs.rs#588)                // verbatim at every consumer's `compile_from_args` body;
[589](https://docs.rs#589)                // the fused primitive names the composition as ONE
[590](https://docs.rs#590)                // substrate-level operation so a regression that drifts
[591](https://docs.rs#591)                // ONE consumer's gate from the others (e.g. a future
[592](https://docs.rs#592)                // emitter swaps the order, a hand-written impl forgets
[593](https://docs.rs#593)                // the second call) is structurally impossible — every
[594](https://docs.rs#594)                // consumer routes through ONE function, every diagnostic
[595](https://docs.rs#595)                // surfaces from ONE call site.
[596](https://docs.rs#596)                let kw = ::tatara_lisp::domain::parse_kwargs_strict(
[597](https://docs.rs#597)                    args,
[598](https://docs.rs#598)                    __TATARA_ALLOWED_KEYWORDS,
[599](https://docs.rs#599)                )?;
[600](https://docs.rs#600)                Ok(Self {
[601](https://docs.rs#601)                    #(#field_inits),*
[602](https://docs.rs#602)                })

[610](https://docs.rs#610)fn extract_keyword(attrs: &[Attribute]) -> Option<String> {
[611](https://docs.rs#611)    for attr in attrs {
[612](https://docs.rs#612)        if !attr.path().is_ident("tatara") {
[613](https://docs.rs#613)            continue;
[614](https://docs.rs#614)        }
[615](https://docs.rs#615)        let Meta::List(list) = &attr.meta else {
[616](https://docs.rs#616)            continue;
[617](https://docs.rs#617)        };
[618](https://docs.rs#618)        let mut found: Option<String> = None;
[619](https://docs.rs#619)        let _ = list.parse_nested_meta(|meta| {
[620](https://docs.rs#620)            if meta.path.is_ident("keyword") {
[621](https://docs.rs#621)                let value = meta.value()?;
[622](https://docs.rs#622)                let s: LitStr = value.parse()?;
[623](https://docs.rs#623)                found = Some(s.value());
[624](https://docs.rs#624)            }
[625](https://docs.rs#625)            Ok(())
[626](https://docs.rs#626)        });
[627](https://docs.rs#627)        if found.is_some() {
[628](https://docs.rs#628)            return found;
[629](https://docs.rs#629)        }
[630](https://docs.rs#630)    }

[651](https://docs.rs#651)/// Check if the field carries `#[serde(default)]` / `#[serde(default = "…")]`.

[654](https://docs.rs#654)fn has_serde_default(field: &syn::Field) -> bool {

[656](https://docs.rs#656)        if !attr.path().is_ident("serde") {

[662](https://docs.rs#662)        let tokens = list.tokens.to_string();
[663](https://docs.rs#663)        if tokens.contains("default") {
[664](https://docs.rs#664)            return true;

[666](https://docs.rs#666)    }

[670](https://docs.rs#670)fn extractor_for(ty: &Type, key: &str, has_default: bool) -> Result<TokenStream2, String> {
[671](https://docs.rs#671)    let kind = classify(ty);
[672](https://docs.rs#672)    let base = match kind {
[673](https://docs.rs#673)        Kind::String => quote! {
[674](https://docs.rs#674)            ::tatara_lisp::domain::extract_string(&kw, #key)?.to_string()
[675](https://docs.rs#675)        },
[676](https://docs.rs#676)        Kind::OptionalString => quote! {
[677](https://docs.rs#677)            ::tatara_lisp::domain::extract_optional_string(&kw, #key)?.map(::std::string::String::from)
[678](https://docs.rs#678)        },
[679](https://docs.rs#679)        Kind::VecString => quote! {
[680](https://docs.rs#680)            ::tatara_lisp::domain::extract_string_list(&kw, #key)?
[681](https://docs.rs#681)        },
[682](https://docs.rs#682)        Kind::Int(rust_ty) => {
[683](https://docs.rs#683)            let cast: TokenStream2 = rust_ty.parse().unwrap();
[684](https://docs.rs#684)            quote! {
[685](https://docs.rs#685)                ::tatara_lisp::domain::extract_int(&kw, #key)? as #cast
[686](https://docs.rs#686)            }
[687](https://docs.rs#687)        }
[688](https://docs.rs#688)        Kind::OptionalInt(rust_ty) => {
[689](https://docs.rs#689)            let cast: TokenStream2 = rust_ty.parse().unwrap();
[690](https://docs.rs#690)            quote! {
[691](https://docs.rs#691)                ::tatara_lisp::domain::extract_optional_int(&kw, #key)?.map(|n| n as #cast)
[692](https://docs.rs#692)            }
[693](https://docs.rs#693)        }
[694](https://docs.rs#694)        Kind::Float(rust_ty) => {
[695](https://docs.rs#695)            let cast: TokenStream2 = rust_ty.parse().unwrap();
[696](https://docs.rs#696)            quote! {
[697](https://docs.rs#697)                ::tatara_lisp::domain::extract_float(&kw, #key)? as #cast
[698](https://docs.rs#698)            }
[699](https://docs.rs#699)        }
[700](https://docs.rs#700)        Kind::OptionalFloat(rust_ty) => {
[701](https://docs.rs#701)            let cast: TokenStream2 = rust_ty.parse().unwrap();
[702](https://docs.rs#702)            quote! {
[703](https://docs.rs#703)                ::tatara_lisp::domain::extract_optional_float(&kw, #key)?.map(|n| n as #cast)
[704](https://docs.rs#704)            }
[705](https://docs.rs#705)        }
[706](https://docs.rs#706)        Kind::Bool => quote! {
[707](https://docs.rs#707)            ::tatara_lisp::domain::extract_bool(&kw, #key)?
[708](https://docs.rs#708)        },
[709](https://docs.rs#709)        Kind::OptionalBool => quote! {
[710](https://docs.rs#710)            ::tatara_lisp::domain::extract_optional_bool(&kw, #key)?
[711](https://docs.rs#711)        },
[712](https://docs.rs#712)        // Fall-through: anything with `serde::Deserialize` works via the
[713](https://docs.rs#713)        // sexp_to_json bridge. Unlocks enums, nested structs, Vec<Struct>.
[714](https://docs.rs#714)        // The boilerplate that used to live here (sexp_to_json +
[715](https://docs.rs#715)        // serde_json::from_value + LispError::Compile shaping, repeated
[716](https://docs.rs#716)        // three times) lives behind these helpers in
[717](https://docs.rs#717)        // `tatara_lisp::domain` so hand-written impls share the same
[718](https://docs.rs#718)        // error path and future diagnostic upgrades land in one place.
[719](https://docs.rs#719)        Kind::Deserialize => quote! {
[720](https://docs.rs#720)            ::tatara_lisp::domain::extract_via_serde(&kw, #key)?
[721](https://docs.rs#721)        },
[722](https://docs.rs#722)        Kind::OptionalDeserialize => quote! {
[723](https://docs.rs#723)            ::tatara_lisp::domain::extract_optional_via_serde(&kw, #key)?
[724](https://docs.rs#724)        },
[725](https://docs.rs#725)        Kind::VecDeserialize => quote! {
[726](https://docs.rs#726)            ::tatara_lisp::domain::extract_vec_via_serde(&kw, #key)?
[727](https://docs.rs#727)        },
[728](https://docs.rs#728)    };
[729](https://docs.rs#729)    // Respect `#[serde(default)]` — wrap extractor with a missing-key short-circuit.
[730](https://docs.rs#730)    Ok(if has_default {
[731](https://docs.rs#731)        quote! {
[732](https://docs.rs#732)            if kw.contains_key(#key) { #base } else { ::std::default::Default::default() }
[733](https://docs.rs#733)        }
[734](https://docs.rs#734)    } else {
[735](https://docs.rs#735)        base
[736](https://docs.rs#736)    })

[740](https://docs.rs#740)enum Kind {
[741](https://docs.rs#741)    String,
[742](https://docs.rs#742)    OptionalString,
[743](https://docs.rs#743)    VecString,
[744](https://docs.rs#744)    Int(&'static str),
[745](https://docs.rs#745)    OptionalInt(&'static str),
[746](https://docs.rs#746)    Float(&'static str),
[747](https://docs.rs#747)    OptionalFloat(&'static str),
[748](https://docs.rs#748)    Bool,
[749](https://docs.rs#749)    OptionalBool,
[750](https://docs.rs#750)    /// Fall-through: any type implementing `serde::Deserialize`.
[751](https://docs.rs#751)    Deserialize,
[752](https://docs.rs#752)    OptionalDeserialize,
[753](https://docs.rs#753)    VecDeserialize,
[754](https://docs.rs#754)}
[755](https://docs.rs#755)
[756](https://docs.rs#756)fn classify(ty: &Type) -> Kind {
[757](https://docs.rs#757)    if let Type::Path(path) = ty {
[758](https://docs.rs#758)        if let Some(last) = path.path.segments.last() {
[759](https://docs.rs#759)            match last.ident.to_string().as_str() {
[760](https://docs.rs#760)                "String" => return Kind::String,
[761](https://docs.rs#761)                "bool" => return Kind::Bool,
[762](https://docs.rs#762)                "i64" => return Kind::Int("i64"),
[763](https://docs.rs#763)                "i32" => return Kind::Int("i32"),
[764](https://docs.rs#764)                "u32" => return Kind::Int("u32"),
[765](https://docs.rs#765)                "u64" => return Kind::Int("u64"),
[766](https://docs.rs#766)                "usize" => return Kind::Int("usize"),
[767](https://docs.rs#767)                "f64" => return Kind::Float("f64"),
[768](https://docs.rs#768)                "f32" => return Kind::Float("f32"),
[769](https://docs.rs#769)                "Option" => return classify_option(last),
[770](https://docs.rs#770)                "Vec" => return classify_vec(last),
[771](https://docs.rs#771)                _ => {}
[772](https://docs.rs#772)            }
[773](https://docs.rs#773)        }
[774](https://docs.rs#774)    }
[775](https://docs.rs#775)    // Anything else: fall through to serde Deserialize.
[776](https://docs.rs#776)    Kind::Deserialize
[777](https://docs.rs#777)}
[778](https://docs.rs#778)
[779](https://docs.rs#779)fn classify_option(last: &syn::PathSegment) -> Kind {
[780](https://docs.rs#780)    let Ok(inner) = first_generic_type(last) else {
[781](https://docs.rs#781)        return Kind::OptionalDeserialize;
[782](https://docs.rs#782)    };
[783](https://docs.rs#783)    match classify(inner) {
[784](https://docs.rs#784)        Kind::String => Kind::OptionalString,
[785](https://docs.rs#785)        Kind::Int(t) => Kind::OptionalInt(t),
[786](https://docs.rs#786)        Kind::Float(t) => Kind::OptionalFloat(t),
[787](https://docs.rs#787)        Kind::Bool => Kind::OptionalBool,
[788](https://docs.rs#788)        _ => Kind::OptionalDeserialize,
[789](https://docs.rs#789)    }
[790](https://docs.rs#790)}
[791](https://docs.rs#791)
[792](https://docs.rs#792)fn classify_vec(last: &syn::PathSegment) -> Kind {
[793](https://docs.rs#793)    let Ok(inner) = first_generic_type(last) else {
[794](https://docs.rs#794)        return Kind::VecDeserialize;
[795](https://docs.rs#795)    };
[796](https://docs.rs#796)    match classify(inner) {
[797](https://docs.rs#797)        Kind::String => Kind::VecString,
[798](https://docs.rs#798)        _ => Kind::VecDeserialize,
[799](https://docs.rs#799)    }
[800](https://docs.rs#800)}
[801](https://docs.rs#801)
[802](https://docs.rs#802)fn first_generic_type(seg: &syn::PathSegment) -> Result<&Type, String> {
[803](https://docs.rs#803)    let syn::PathArguments::AngleBracketed(args) = &seg.arguments else {
[804](https://docs.rs#804)        return Err("expected <T> generic arguments".into());
[805](https://docs.rs#805)    };
[806](https://docs.rs#806)    for arg in &args.args {
[807](https://docs.rs#807)        if let syn::GenericArgument::Type(t) = arg {
[808](https://docs.rs#808)            return Ok(t);
[809](https://docs.rs#809)        }
[810](https://docs.rs#810)    }
[811](https://docs.rs#811)    Err("no type argument found".into())
[812](https://docs.rs#812)}

# ClosedSet in tatara_lisp_derive - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tatara-lisp-derive/0.2.124/tatara_lisp_derive/derive.ClosedSet.html

```
#[derive(ClosedSet)]
{
    // Attributes available to this derive:
    #[closed_set]
}
```
## Expand description

`#[derive(ClosedSet)]` — emit the substrate-wide
[`tatara_lisp::ClosedSet`] impl + the matching [ std::str::FromStr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/str/traits/trait.FromStr.html)
delegation for any enum carrying the closed-set-enum idiom (the
four-piece

`ALL` + projection + `Unknown` + `FromStr` shape).Lifts the 4-line `impl ClosedSet` + 4-line `impl FromStr` boilerplate
that 29+ workspace-wide implementors re-derive byte-for-byte — the
per-implementor content stays at the inherent `ALL` constant and the
inherent projection method (`as_str`, `label`, `prefix`, `marker`,
`keyword`, …), while the trait-impl plumbing collapses onto ONE
derive line.

[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)Attributes

- `#[closed_set(via = "as_str")]`— name of the inherent projection method the trait’s [- `tatara_lisp::ClosedSet::label`] delegates to. Defaults to- `"label"`. Domain-canonical names (- `tatara_process`’s- `as_str`,- `tatara_lisp::ast::QuoteForm::prefix`,- `tatara_lisp::error::UnquoteForm::marker`,- `tatara_lisp::error::MacroDefHead::keyword`) stay load-bearing.
- `#[closed_set(unknown = "UnknownX")]`— name of the per-implementor- `Unknown`carrier struct [- `tatara_lisp::ClosedSet::make_unknown`] constructs. Defaults to- `"Unknown{EnumName}"`— matches the substrate-wide naming convention (- `UnknownChannelKind`for- `ChannelKind`).
- `#[closed_set(no_from_str)]`— suppress the generated- `impl FromStr`. Use for enums that already carry a bespoke- `FromStr`shape (e.g. [- `tatara_lisp::error::CompilerSpecIoStage`]’s compound- `"{operation}: {label}"`key, which keys on a projection PAIR rather than a single label).
- `#[closed_set(generate_unknown)]`/- `#[closed_set(generate_unknown = "<label>")]`— emit the- `pub struct Unknown{EnumName}(pub String)`parse-rejection carrier alongside the trait impl. The carrier derives- `Debug + Clone + PartialEq + Eq + thiserror::Error`and renders- `#[error("unknown <label>: {0}")]`. The bare form derives- `<label>`by spacing the PascalCase enum name into lowercase words (- `ChannelKind`→ “channel kind”,- `ReplacementPolicy`→ “replacement policy”); the- `= "..."`form pins an explicit label for irregular cases (- `MacroDefHead`wants “macro definition head” rather than the auto-derived “macro def head”;- `MustReachPhase`wants “must-reach phase”). The 3-line- `pub struct Unknown{EnumName}(pub String)`declaration (plus its thiserror derives +- `#[error(...)]`annotation) is the substrate-wide closed-set-enum idiom’s last hand-rolled piece; this attribute collapses it onto the derive so a 40+ enum cohort emits the carrier through ONE generative shape rather than re-deriving the boilerplate at each declaration site.
- `#[closed_set(display)]`— emit the substrate-wide- `impl ::core::fmt::Display for $name { f.write_str(Self::$via(*self)) }`block alongside the trait impl. The 5-line Display block (the- `impl fmt::Display`, the- `fn fmt`, the- `f.write_str(self.$via())`body) appears 28+ times across- `tatara-process`/- `tatara-lisp`byte-for-byte — every closed-set carrier on a PascalCase wire-format axis composes its operator-facing diagnostic through Display rather than through a hard-coded literal that would silently rot when a variant gets renamed. The attribute collapses the 5-line block onto ONE flag so the- `as_str`⇄ Display ⇄- `FromStr`triad emits through ONE generative shape per closed-set enum. The emission requires- `Self: ::core::marker::Copy`(the- `ClosedSet`trait already requires it). Set the flag in combination with- `via`to pin Display onto the inherent projection rather than the trait method; without the flag the implementor keeps its hand-rolled Display block (e.g. for a bespoke Display shape like [- `tatara_process::lifetime_clock::TerminateReason`]’s structured-reason formatter).

[§](https://docs.rs#implementor-requirements)Implementor requirements

The derive expects the enum to expose at the inherent surface:

- `pub const ALL: [Self; N] = [...]`— forced-arity array literal.
- A `fn projection(self) -> &'static str`method whose name matches`via`(defaults to`label`).
- A `pub struct UnknownX(pub String)`in the same module whose name matches`unknown`(defaults to`Unknown{EnumName}`) — UNLESS`#[closed_set(generate_unknown)]`is set, in which case the derive emits the struct itself.

The derive emits:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
impl ::tatara_lisp::ClosedSet for $name {
    const ALL: &'static [Self] = &Self::ALL;
    type Unknown = $unknown;
    fn label(self) -> &'static str { Self::$via(self) }
    fn make_unknown(s: &str) -> Self::Unknown {
        $unknown(::std::string::String::from(s))
    }
}
impl ::core::str::FromStr for $name {
    type Err = $unknown;
    fn from_str(s: &str) -> ::core::result::Result<Self, Self::Err> {
        <Self as ::tatara_lisp::ClosedSet>::parse_label(s)
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#theory-grounding)Theory grounding

THEORY.md §VI.1 — generation over composition; the derive IS the
generative shape — new closed-set enums add ONE `#[derive(ClosedSet)]`
line + the attribute that names their inherent projection method
instead of re-deriving the eight-line `impl ClosedSet` + `impl FromStr`
pair byte-for-byte. The per-implementor `Unknown` carrier stays
hand-rolled (its `#[error("unknown <thing>: {0}")]` annotation IS
per-implementor content), but the trait-impl plumbing it threads
through collapses onto the derive.

---

# phoxal 0.22.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/phoxal/0.22.0

# phoxal

A production-oriented framework for autonomous robots, shipped as one crate.

Phoxal gives a robot a small, strongly-typed core: a contract bus over Zenoh, a single dated API-version contract set, and a derive-based participant authoring model. The framework owns the awkward parts - argument parsing, bus connection, scheduling, query serving, shutdown, and health - so the code you write is the robot's behavior, not its plumbing.

Greenfield rewrite in progress(`tmp/framework-rewrite`). The bus + participant machinery and the macros are new; the official service/simulator/tool crates are being re-ported onto this surface and some are temporarily out of the workspace.

```
[]
 = "0.17"      # the engine: runner, derives, SetupContext, prelude
 = "0.17"  # the contract tree: `use phoxal_api::y2026_1 as api;`
```
## The authoring model

A service is **one struct of typed handles + one annotated inherent impl**.
The struct declares the contracts it uses (as handle fields) and the one API version it runs against; the impl declares the lifecycle.

```
use y2026_1 as api;
use *;
```
Key rules the example shows:

- Import exactly one dated API module (`use phoxal_api::y2026_1 as api;`) and declare it on the derive (`#[phoxal(api = y2026_1)]`,**mandatory**).
- Handle fields use version-local bodies: `Publisher<api::drive::Target>`,`Latest<api::drive::State>`. The derive emits a`ContractBody<Api = R::Api>`assertion, so a body from another API version is a**compile error**.
- Topics are api-local: `api::topic::new().drive().state()`.
- The wire body is the plain payload; `api_version`, family, and codec ride bus metadata. Normal participants never open Zenoh - the runner opens the bundle-selected bus profile before`#[setup]`.
- `config`is for- **user participants only**. Official participants take no- `config`param and read the robot model through- `ctx.robot()`.
- `cargo run --example runtime_control_loop emit-apis`prints the participant's static metadata as one JSON document (the- `emit-apis`subcommand) and exits.

The runner also owns the rest of the lifecycle: `#[step(hz = ...)]` is the scheduled control loop, `#[server]` / `#[server_snapshot]` serve queries, and `#[shutdown]` runs graceful park/stop/flush before the bus closes.

## Modules

A participant depends on two crates: the `phoxal` engine (the modules below) and the `phoxal-api` contract tree.

| Module | What it is |
|---|---|
| `phoxal_api`(separate crate) | The dated API-version modules ( `phoxal_api::y2026_1`, …) generated by`phoxal_api_tree!`from a tree of nested nodes: the marker`enum Api`(`ApiVersion`), version-local wire bodies + their`ContractBody`impls, and the api-local`topic`builders. Imported directly with`use phoxal_api::y2026_1 as api;`. |
| [ `phoxal::prelude`] | Everything a participant author imports with `use phoxal::prelude::*;`: the handle types,`SetupContext`/`StepContext`, and`Result`. |
| [ `phoxal::bus`] | Re-export of the `phoxal-bus`crate (the ABI floor): the Zenoh-native`bus_abi`boundary: the key scheme`<namespace>/robots/<robot-id>/<topic>`, the MessagePack codec, the`BusMetadata`attachment, and the body-typed handles`Publisher`/`Subscriber`/`Latest`/`Querier`. |
| [ `phoxal::participant`] | The static metadata traits the macros target, `SetupContext`/`StepContext`/`ShutdownContext`, the clock (`RealClock`/`TestClock`) + scheduler,`ParticipantLaunch`,`emit-apis`, and the runner (`run`/`tokio::run`). |
| [ `phoxal::model`] | Authored manifest schemas ( `robot.yaml`,`structure.urdf`,`component.yaml`, …). |

## Authoring the API tree

The `phoxal_api` modules (in the `phoxal-api` crate) are generated by `phoxal_api_tree!` from a tree of **nested nodes**.
A node is `name { … }` (static) or `name(var) { … }` (dynamic, where `var` is a key segment filled at build time), nestable to any depth.
A node body holds any mix of `struct`/`enum` type declarations, `topic` declarations, and child nodes.
Each topic declares a **role**: `topic <leaf>: command <Body>;` (a control input the owning service subscribes), `topic <leaf>: state <Body>;` (telemetry the owning service publishes), or `topic <leaf>: query <Req> => <Resp>;` (request/response).
`command` and `state` are both pub/sub on the wire; the role selects the side brand of the generated builders (L1), so the public client builder (`api::topic::new()`) and the `internal` owner builder (`api::topic::internal::new(cap)`) return different branded topics (`Publish`/`Subscribe`) and taking the wrong side does not compile.
The owner builder additionally requires the runner-minted `OwnerCap` (L2): pass `ctx.owner_capability()`, so owning a topic is a deliberate, capability-gated opt-in rather than something that can happen by accident.
There are no key-template strings and no topic parameter lists; dynamism comes entirely from the `(var)` nodes on the path.

```
phoxal_api_tree!
```
Everything a topic exposes is **derived from the node path** `n1 … nk` to its leaf (each `ni` has a `name` and an optional `var`):

- **Topic key**(- `ContractBody::TOPIC`, versionless): each node emits- `name`, or- `name/{var}`for a dynamic node, joined by- `/`, then- `/<leaf>`. So- `drive`→- `target`is- `drive/target`, and- `component(instance)`→- `motor(capability)`→- `command`is- `component/{instance}/motor/{capability}/command`.
- **Module path / type location**: each node becomes a nested- `pub mod name`, and a node's types + their- `ContractBody`impls live in that module. Variables never appear in the module path, so the body above is- `phoxal_api::y2026_1::component::motor::Command`.
- **FAMILY**(- `ContractBody::FAMILY`): the node names joined by- `::`, then- `::TypeName`- e.g.- `drive::Target`,- `component::motor::Command`.
- **Builder**:- `api::topic::new().n1(var?)…nk(var?).leaf()`. A dynamic node's method takes its var as- `impl Display`(- `*`/- `**`stay valid for subscribe); the leaf method yields the typed- `Topic`. So- `api::topic::new().component("front_left").motor("drive").command()`builds the key- `component/front_left/motor/drive/command`.

Each node is **self-contained**: it declares its own copy of every type it uses, with **no  super::** and no shared/common module.
Because the node path disambiguates, names are path-local -

`component::imu::Sample` and `component::range::Sample` are distinct types that may safely repeat field names.
Duplicating an identical type across sibling nodes is intentional, not a smell.A later `version yNNNN_M extends yNNNN_K { … }` re-emits the parent tree as **fresh types** under the child version (same FAMILY/TOPIC, a different `Api`), overriding a type by ident or a topic by leaf and appending wholly new nodes - so an inherited node never needs to be retyped.

## Entrypoints

- Default (blocking): `fn main() -> phoxal::Result<()> { phoxal::run::<R>() }`.
- Advanced (async): `phoxal::tokio::run::<R>().await`for custom Tokio mains.

## Official service set

The complete platform participant set ships alongside this crate in the workspace `service/` tree (`drive`, `localize`, `map`, `safety`, …).
They are full official participants authored on exactly this surface, and they double as worked reference reading.
Neutral teaching examples live in `phoxal/examples/` (`runtime_control_loop`, `runtime_query_server`, `runtime_snapshot_server`, `runtime_async_entrypoint`).

## Status

Pre-1.0, building in public.
One API version per robot graph (`#[phoxal(api = y2026_1)]`); the wire body is the plain payload and the version identity rides bus metadata, never the key.
Compatibility is checked at build/check time (`emit-apis` + `phoxal-cli check`), never by introspecting a running binary.

## License

AGPL-3.0-only. A commercial license is available - see the repository.

# anyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/anyhow/^1.0.102/

## Expand description

This library provides [ anyhow::Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html), a trait object based error
type for easy idiomatic error handling in Rust applications.

[§](https://docs.rs#details)Details

-
Use `Result<T, anyhow::Error>`, or equivalently`anyhow::Result<T>`, as the return type of any fallible function.Within the function, use `?`to easily propagate any error that implements the`std::error::Error``use anyhow::Result; fn get_cluster_info() -> Result<ClusterMap> { let config = std::fs::read_to_string("cluster.json")?; let map: ClusterMap = serde_json::from_str(&config)?; Ok(map) }`
-
Attach context to help the person troubleshooting the error understand where things went wrong. A low-level error like “No such file or directory” can be annoying to debug without more context about what higher level step the application was in the middle of. `use anyhow::{Context, Result}; fn main() -> Result<()> { ... it.detach().context("Failed to detach the important thing")?; let content = std::fs::read(path) .with_context(|| format!("Failed to read instrs from {}", path))?; ... }``Error: Failed to read instrs from ./path/to/instrs.json Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)`
-
Downcasting is supported and can be by value, by shared reference, or by mutable reference as needed. `// If the error was caused by redaction, then return a // tombstone instead of the content. match root_cause.downcast_ref::<DataStoreError>() { Some(DataStoreError::Censored(_)) => Ok(Poll::Ready(REDACTED_CONTENT)), None => Err(error), }`
-
If using Rust ≥ 1.65, a backtrace is captured and printed with the error if the underlying error type does not already provide its own. In order to see backtraces, they must be enabled through the environment variables described in `std::backtrace`- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
`RUST_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only errors to have backtraces, set `RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only panics to have backtraces, set `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`and`RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=0`.

- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
-
Anyhow works with any error type that has an impl of `std::error::Error`, including ones defined in your crate. We do not bundle a`derive(Error)`macro but you can write the impls yourself or use a standalone macro like[thiserror](https://github.com/dtolnay/thiserror).`use thiserror::Error; #[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum FormatError { #[error("Invalid header (expected {expected:?}, got {found:?})")] InvalidHeader { expected: String, found: String, }, #[error("Missing attribute: {0}")] MissingAttribute(String), }`
-
One-off error messages can be constructed using the `anyhow!`macro, which supports string interpolation and produces an`anyhow::Error`.`return Err(anyhow!("Missing attribute: {}", missing));`A `bail!`macro is provided as a shorthand for the same early return.`bail!("Missing attribute: {}", missing);`

[§](https://docs.rs#no-std-support)No-std support

In no_std mode, almost all of the same API is available and works the same way. To depend on Anyhow in no_std mode, disable our default enabled “std” feature in Cargo.toml. A global allocator is required.

```
[dependencies]
anyhow = { version = "1.0", default-features = false }
```
With versions of Rust older than 1.81, no_std mode may require an additional
`.map_err(Error::msg)` when working with a non-Anyhow error type inside a
function that returns Anyhow’s error type, as the trait that `?`-based error
conversions are defined by is only available in std in those old versions.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [anyhow](https://docs.rs/macro.anyhow.html)as format_err;

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [anyhow](https://docs.rs/macro.anyhow.html)
- Construct an ad-hoc error from a string or existing non-`anyhow`error value.
- [bail](https://docs.rs/macro.bail.html)
- Return early with an error.
- [ensure](https://docs.rs/macro.ensure.html)
- Return early with an error if a condition is not satisfied.

# arc_swap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/arc-swap/^1.9.1/

## Expand description

Making [ Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html) itself atomic

The [ ArcSwap](https://docs.rs/type.ArcSwap.html) type is a container for an

`Arc` that can be changed atomically. Semantically,
it is similar to something like `Atomic<Arc<T>>` (if there was such a thing) or
`RwLock<Arc<T>>` (but without the need for the locking). It is optimized for read-mostly
scenarios, with consistent performance characteristics.[§](https://docs.rs#motivation)Motivation

There are many situations in which one might want to have some data structure that is often read and seldom updated. Some examples might be a configuration of a service, routing tables, snapshot of some data that is renewed every few minutes, etc.

In all these cases one needs:

- Being able to read the current value of the data structure, fast, often and concurrently from many threads.
- Using the same version of the data structure over longer period of time ‒ a query should be answered by a consistent version of data, a packet should be routed either by an old or by a new version of the routing table but not by a combination, etc.
- Perform an update without disrupting the processing.

The first idea would be to use [ RwLock<T>](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/struct.RwLock.html) and keep a read-lock for the whole time of
processing. Update would, however, pause all processing until done.

Better option would be to have [ RwLock<Arc<T>>](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/struct.RwLock.html). Then one would lock, clone the

[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)and unlock. This suffers from CPU-level contention (on the lock and on the reference count of the

[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)) which makes it relatively slow. Depending on the implementation, an update may be blocked for arbitrary long time by a steady inflow of readers.

```
static ROUTING_TABLE: Lazy<RwLock<Arc<RoutingTable>>> = Lazy::new(|| {
    RwLock::new(Arc::new(RoutingTable))
});
fn process_packet(packet: Packet) {
    let table = Arc::clone(&ROUTING_TABLE.read().unwrap());
    table.route(packet);
}
```
The [ArcSwap](https://docs.rs/type.ArcSwap.html) can be used instead, which solves the above problems and has better performance
characteristics than the [RwLock](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/sync/struct.RwLock.html), both in contended and non-contended scenarios.

```
static ROUTING_TABLE: Lazy<ArcSwap<RoutingTable>> = Lazy::new(|| {
    ArcSwap::from_pointee(RoutingTable)
});
fn process_packet(packet: Packet) {
    let table = ROUTING_TABLE.load();
    table.route(packet);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#crate-contents)Crate contents

At the heart of the crate there are [ ArcSwap](https://docs.rs/type.ArcSwap.html) and

[types, containers for an](https://docs.rs/type.ArcSwapOption.html)

`ArcSwapOption`[and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)

`Arc`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)

`Option<Arc>`Technically, these are type aliases for partial instantiations of the [ ArcSwapAny](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcSwapAny.html) type. The

[is more flexible and allows tweaking of many things (can store other things than](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcSwapAny.html)

`ArcSwapAny`[s, can configure the locking](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)

`Arc`[). For details about the tweaking, see the documentation of the](https://docs.rs/strategy/trait.Strategy.html)

`Strategy`[module and the](https://docs.rs/strategy/index.html)

`strategy`[trait.](https://docs.rs/trait.RefCnt.html)

`RefCnt`The [ cache](https://docs.rs/cache/index.html) module provides means for speeding up read access of the contained data at the
cost of delayed reclamation.

The [ access](https://docs.rs/access/index.html) module can be used to do projections into the contained data to separate parts
of application from each other (eg. giving a component access to only its own part of
configuration while still having it reloaded as a whole).

[§](https://docs.rs#before-using)Before using

The data structure is a bit niche. Before using, please check the
[limitations and common pitfalls](https://docs.rs/docs/limitations/index.html) and the [performance
characteristics](https://docs.rs/docs/performance/index.html), including choosing the right [read
operation](https://docs.rs/docs/performance/index.html#read-operations).

You can also get an inspiration about what’s possible in the [common patterns](https://docs.rs/docs/patterns/index.html)
section.

[§](https://docs.rs#release-19)Release 1.9

Unfortunately, several orderings were too weak in the original code (proofs based on wrong assumptions / wrong reading of the standard). The 1.9 version should fix them, but probably introduces some performance degradation.

I hope to re-design and rewrite from scratch eventually, with less amount of SeqCst needed.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use std::sync::Arc;
use arc_swap::ArcSwap;
use crossbeam_utils::thread;
let config = ArcSwap::from(Arc::new(String::default()));
thread::scope(|scope| {
    scope.spawn(|_| {
        let new_conf = Arc::new("New configuration".to_owned());
        config.store(new_conf);
    });
    for _ in 0..10 {
        scope.spawn(|_| {
            loop {
                let cfg = config.load();
                if !cfg.is_empty() {
                    assert_eq!(**cfg, "New configuration");
                    return;
                }
            }
        });
    }
}).unwrap();
```

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap/^4.6.1/

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#related-projects)Related Projects

Augment clap:

- [wild](https://crates.io/crates/wild)for supporting wildcards (- `*`) on Windows like you do Linux
- [argfile](https://crates.io/crates/argfile)for loading additional arguments from a file (aka response files)
- [shadow-rs](https://crates.io/crates/shadow-rs)for generating- `Command::long_version`
- [clap_mangen](https://crates.io/crates/clap_mangen)for generating man page source (roff)
- [clap_complete](https://crates.io/crates/clap_complete)for shell completion support
- [clap-i18n-richformatter](https://crates.io/crates/clap-i18n-richformatter)for i18n support with- `clap::error::RichFormatter`

CLI Helpers

- [clio](https://crates.io/crates/clio)for reading/writing to files specified as arguments
